gems_verified_6_ready_to_ship.name: The tap de Cadaqués
gems_verified_6_ready_to_ship.story: Cork-shaped sugar-dusted sponge named for the tap (cork) of a cava bottle it apes when it rises past its mould. La Mallorquina — the Cabrisas family pastisseria by the church since the 1700s — is the only maker; taps made there since the 1800s. Sources: TERMCAT 'tap de Cadaqués'; Catavino; M'agrada Catalunya. where: La Mallorquina, Plaça Doctor Trèmols.

gems_verified_6_ready_to_ship.name: Dalí's dinners at Portlligat
gems_verified_6_ready_to_ship.story: Dalí lived in Portlligat, the cove over the headland; his 1973 cookbook Les Dîners de Gala set down 136 recipes from the surrealist banquets he and Gala staged there — food as spectacle, born on this shore. Sources: NPR/Smithsonian/TASCHEN. where: Portlligat — Casa-Museu Salvador Dalí.

gems_verified_6_ready_to_ship.name: The sweet Garnatxa
gems_verified_6_ready_to_ship.story: Sweet fortified solera wine from overripe Garnatxa, off the slate terraces of DO Empordà (granted 1972; terraces first tended by the monks of Sant Pere de Rodes). Sources: winetourism.com; costabrava.org; empordaturisme. where: DO Empordà cellars, Cap de Creus.

gems_verified_6_ready_to_ship.name: Suquet — the at-sea stew
gems_verified_6_ready_to_ship.story: Not a Cadaqués invention but a Cadaqués habit: the pot fishermen cooked over days at sea, catch dropped in with the tomato/onion/potato/garlic carried from shore. Honest regional framing. where: harbour tavernes.

gems_verified_6_ready_to_ship.name: The sea-urchin winter
gems_verified_6_ready_to_ship.story: The eriçó de mar cracked open raw with bread and cold white wine when the cold water clears. HONEST CORRECTION: the garoinada festival with tasting menus belongs down-coast in Palafrugell/Baix Empordà (mid-Jan–March); here it is just the urchin in season. Sources: costabrava.org; femturisme; moll.company. where: winter tables (and Palafrugell, down-coast).

gems_verified_6_ready_to_ship.name: The salting art from Empúries
gems_verified_6_ready_to_ship.story: Greeks at Empúries perfected fish-salting here; the Romans built a garum works. HONEST CORRECTION: the famous salt-cured anxova is l'Escala's craft (Solés 1888, Callol i Serrats 1847), not Cadaqués's own — here the anchovy is landed and eaten more fresh than cured. Sources: Smithsonian anchovy-coast; barcelona-metropolitan; fascinatingspain. where: the Alt Empordà coast.

gems_verified_7_ready_to_ship.story: The saint's-day pasta: sporki makaruli ('dirty macaroni') is macaroni dragged through a long-simmered beef-and-red-wine sugo darkened with grape molasses, prunes, clove, nutmeg and cinnamon, eaten above all on 3 February, the feast of St Blaise, Dubrovnik's patron. gems_verified_7_ready_to_ship.story: Croatia's first cru: Dingac, the perilously steep south-facing Peljesac slope where Plavac Mali ripens over the sea, became in 1961 the first Croatian wine protected by law (registered under the Geneva Convention) after falsifications of its name grew rife. Barely ~80 ha; the grapes were long carried out by donkey. Its sibling Postup and the wider Plavac Mali are the peninsula's kings, poured across Dubrovnik. Sources: en.wikipedia.org 'Dingac'; wineandmore.com; croatian.wine. where: Peljesac cellars (Grgic Vina, Milos Stagnum) and Dubrovnik wine bars (D'vino).

gems_verified_7_ready_to_ship.story: Not the Sicilian rice ball: in Dubrovnik arancini (narancini) are candied strips of wild-orange peel, slow-cooked in sugar until glassy. Wild bitter oranges leaned against the stone walls of the Republic's Renaissance monastery gardens and summer villas; at grape-and-quince harvest the women of Dubrovnik candied their peel into this fragrant sweet. HONEST DISAMBIGUATION: same name, different food from Sicily's fried risotto balls. gems_verified_7_ready_to_ship.story: The salt that built a republic: Solana Ston is the oldest working saltworks in Europe, its 58 sun-and-wind evaporation pans laid over Roman foundations (the Romans named the marsh Stagnum). When the Dubrovnik Republic founded Ston and Mali Ston in 1333 and walled them, Ston salt became its single most valuable export — at times a third of the Republic's wealth — still hand-raked April to October, some pans floored with granite that once salted the Viennese court. Sources: solanaston.hr 'The History'; Fodor's Solana Ston; In Your Pocket 'Croatian Paths of Salt'. where: Ston, base of the Peljesac walls.
